::: {.why}
Fast is not a property, it is a set of specific durations, and knowing them separates a sensible statement about what you can and cannot do from a vague one.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State the latency of a cache reference, a memory reference, an SSD read, a data centre round trip and a Chicago to New York round trip, to an order of magnitude.
- Say which of your own operations are bounded by which of those, measured rather than guessed.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Check your five guesses and fix the wrong ones, then add three more: a network round trip within a rack, a Python function call, and a numpy operation on a thousand-element array. Write all eight on one card with the units aligned so the ratios are visible.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Measure your own stack: time your signal computation, your order submission round trip to the paper broker, and your data pull. Then place them on the same scale as the eight reference numbers. Your submission round trip is probably five orders of magnitude above the exchange's matching time, and knowing that number precisely is what makes tomorrow's argument concrete.
:::
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Roughly how long does an L1 cache reference take, a main memory reference, a random SSD read and a data centre round trip? Now say why that changes how you would store a tick database.
:::
